question: Does the installed writable Google My Drive mount handle a broader real-application and provider-observation matrix on the owner's existing connection?
kind: Explicitly authorized bounded live functional validation on one run-owned Google Drive folder.
authorization: The owner asked for further tests with the current Google Drive connection. Earlier in this session the owner explicitly authorized Google Drive read and write operations. Every mutation in this run is confined to one newly created, uniquely named folder and cleanup is by its exact provider identity.
command: A bounded operator-driven sequence using the installed cirrove CLI, the mounted path, LibreOffice 26.8 headless conversion, and the ignored exact-ID Google live helpers. No recursive filesystem deletion is used.
scope: The enabled account labelled google and one new top-level folder named Cirrove Acceptance 2026-09-20 2119. Existing user items are read only by the aggregate GET-only validator; it emits no names, ids, hashes or bodies.
arms: Run the aggregate GET-only Google validator against eight bounded binary files and all indexed shortcut targets, comparing direct provider bytes with mounted bytes.
Write a deterministic 20 MiB-plus binary through the ordinary mount, wait for writeback, and compare its exact provider bytes by SHA-256.
Have LibreOffice read a local source and create real ODT and DOCX outputs in the mounted folder, then verify both settled remotely and their exact provider bytes match the mounted files.
Exercise held-descriptor atomic replacement: an old open descriptor must retain the old bytes while the replaced path exposes and uploads the new bytes.
Rename one exact run-owned file through the provider adapter, measure when the mounted view follows it, then edit the observed new path and verify exact remote bytes.
Pin the large run-owned file until resident, restart neither daemon nor mount, read it again, unpin it, and verify the reservation is released.
Trash only the exact registered run-owned tree through the bounded provider helper and return the ordinary account to ready with zero failed or stuck changes.
prediction: All bounded reads will match; the large and LibreOffice outputs will upload without stuck work; held-descriptor replacement will preserve old and new streams; an external exact-ID rename will appear through polling within 90 seconds; the renamed file will remain writable; pinning will reach full residency and unpin cleanly; exact-ID cleanup will leave no run-owned mount path.
endpoint: Pass an arm only with an independently observable result: byte equality or exact SHA-256 for content, old/new descriptor equality for replacement, elapsed visibility for external rename, resident bytes and released reservation for pinning, and exact-ID absence plus zero failed/stuck changes for cleanup. A failure is recorded rather than retried into a pass.
limits: One account and one bounded run do not establish general reliability. The run cannot validate Shared Drives, OAuth publication, Google-native document import/export, push notifications, full offline operation or large-library longevity. Provider polling is accepted for the external-change arm.

observations.arm: aggregate GET-only comparison, first registered execution
observations.outcome: FAIL: 0 compared, 8 classified as changed, 0 classified unavailable; one indexed shortcut target was missing.
observations.interpretation: The existing aggregate combined direct-provider version changes, direct absence and mounted byte mismatches under one changed_files counter, so this result is real but not diagnostic enough to attribute.
observations.next_step: Split only the aggregate counters, demonstrate that the same unit suite passes, then run a diagnostic follow-up. The first execution remains the registered result and is not rewritten as a pass.

observations.arm: diagnostic GET-only follow-up using an exact current node before each content read
observations.outcome: PASS for bytes: 8 of 8 files, 23,147 bytes, zero byte mismatches and zero unavailable reads. All eight indexed nodes carried older content and metadata versions, with zero namespace differences. One indexed shortcut target was already missing at Google.
observations.interpretation: The existing index was created with the earlier google-version content lineage. The current adapter uses binary headRevisionId. Exact current metadata and mounted reads agree; the stale upgrade metadata is visible and lazily healed rather than a data mismatch.

observations.arm: 20 MiB-plus mounted write and exact provider readback
observations.outcome: PASS: 20,971,643 bytes crossed the normal mount in one new queue entry. Mounted and direct Google reads both matched SHA-256 bf8d051848d6b9bda46d10fe091db2d9aa2a7439d97eca361583c1880abbaedd; zero failed or stuck changes.
observations.helper_correction: The exact-ID live readback helper originally requested the whole file in one call although the adapter limit is 8 MiB. It now hashes bounded 4 MiB chunks; this changes only the validator and made the large independent readback possible.

observations.outcome: PASS after a recorded setup correction: LibreOffice created an ODT directly in the mount, then read that mounted ODT and created a DOCX beside it. Twelve new journal operations completed; exact Google readback matched both mounted SHA-256 values.
observations.setup_correction: The first HTML-to-DOCX command was rejected locally by LibreOffice because that input/filter pair has no export filter. No DOCX reached Cirrove. The corrected ODT-to-DOCX path exercises a mounted read and mounted write and is the application arm being claimed.

observations.arm: held descriptor, atomic replacement and exact provider readback
observations.outcome: PASS: an open descriptor retained the 37 old bytes while the replaced path exposed 60 new bytes. Five queue operations completed and direct Google readback matched SHA-256 52fdfe598f52f4ff3ed54fd3111df21ec3912f434d752886b3b8a780378557c4.

observations.arm: external exact-ID rename, polling visibility and subsequent mounted edit
observations.outcome: PASS: the Google-side rename became visible after 8,263 ms under its collision-safe ID-qualified name. A mounted O_TRUNC edit through that observed path completed in one queue entry and exact Google readback matched SHA-256 97fdd35315207348260a6dbb0621de7441570b4f146127b97124a00293342032.

observations.arm: pin and file-manager path state for a newly created natural-name file
observations.outcome: FAIL by visible path: both `cirrove pin --path` and `cirrove paths` returned `remote item not found`. Pinning the same exact item ID fetched all 20,971,643 bytes into six blocks and unpin released the reservation. Exact-ID tree cleanup then passed.
observations.cause: The control socket resolved paths only through provider-indexed ID-qualified Google names. FUSE separately overlaid the durable natural names retained for acknowledged mounted creates, so the file manager and pin controls did not resolve the path they visibly presented.

correction.implementation: Writable control requests now resolve visible paths through the same provider-neutral writeback overlay as FUSE. Pin, unpin and batched path-state requests receive the confirmed provider scope and item after that resolution. Read-only mounts retain the existing index resolver.
correction.negative_control: The real-manager kernel regression failed without the correction with `remote item not found` for the natural Google-style path.
correction.positive_control: With the correction restored, the same test accepts the pin, records its reservation, returns a direct pin state for the same visible path, and unpins it through that path.
correction.live_retest: PASS on the installed candidate: a newly mounted 5,243,003-byte file resolved through its visible natural path. Pin completed with 5,243,067 bytes reserved and resident in two blocks; paths reported the same file directly pinned; unpin through the same visible path released the reservation after asynchronous state propagation. Direct Google readback matched SHA-256 8b64de48d04c9850121882be0a70525647e957957b3372b5c94068f6b9b5ddbe.

first_run_cleanup: The exact-ID helper trashed only provider folder 1AJL35q5H_8LTv3uczp7UyhlAOr_-ij7y after unpin. Its mounted path disappeared; the account returned ready with zero failed/stuck changes and no pins.

correction_retest.command: Install the fully checked candidate, create one uniquely named folder and deterministic file through the Google mount, wait for writeback, pin and query the file by its visible natural path, unpin by that same path, then trash only the exact recorded provider folder ID.
correction_retest.prediction: The formerly failing visible path resolves through the writeback overlay; pin reaches full residency, paths reports a direct pin without refusal, unpin releases the reservation, and exact-ID cleanup returns the account to ready with zero failed or stuck changes.
correction_retest.endpoint: Pass only if public CLI commands succeed for the visible natural path and cleanup is independently observed. Record exact bytes, reservation state, cleanup and account health.
correction_retest.path_resolution: The public pin, paths and unpin CLI requests all succeeded with the visible natural mount-relative path.
correction_retest.direct_readback: The exact-ID Google adapter read matched the registered SHA-256.
correction_retest.cleanup: The bounded helper trashed only the recorded correction-run folder ID. Its mount path disappeared; Google returned ready with no pins, failed uploads or stuck changes.

full_project_check.coverage: formatting, clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, kernel groups, script tests, Dolphin plugin build/tests, acceptance ledger and documentation
